ko.executive_summary: PMIC/BCD foundry capacity is experiencing demand compression as AI workloads crowd out mature-node allocation at leading-edge fabs (TSMC, Samsung), creating a window for mature-node specialists (SMIC, Hua Hong) to capture legacy product orders and gain pricing power. SMIC reports record revenue and margin expansion driven by China-onshoring trends and foreign client reallocation, though US equipment export restrictions introduce supply-chain friction for node capacity scaling.
key_facts: SMIC April-June net profit increased 3.6-fold on AI demand and localization momentum
Leadtrend gross margin rebounded to 33.6% as AI crowds out mature process capacity
SMIC China revenue surged 22% in Q2
SMIC reports record revenue with foreign clients shifting orders back to China
TSMC and Samsung shifting to advanced nodes, creating 8-inch demand opening for SMIC and Hua Hong
SMIC flagged US equipment supply delays

implications.text: Tier-1 fab retreat from mature nodes (TSMC, Samsung focus on advanced nodes) is accelerating BCD/8-inch capacity capture by China specialists, reducing global competitive pressure on pricing and easing supply-tightness for PMIC designers.

Leadtrend's 33.6% gross margin rebound and SMIC's record revenue signals demand elasticity recovery in mature-node PMIC; customers onshoring to China and consolidating supply chains are accepting higher ASPs.

SMIC's flagged US equipment delays are a headwind for scaling 8-inch capacity; continued export restrictions could constrain mature-node supply growth and cede long-term advantage to non-US fabs in automotive/server-grade PMIC qualification pipelines.

No explicit certification/qualification news in headlines; opportunity to monitor whether China fabs (SMIC, Hua Hong) are pursuing automotive-grade or server-grade PMIC credentials to lock in higher-margin segments.

ko.counterpoint: PMIC demand surge may be temporary if AI capex cycle moderates; mature-node specialists lack advanced-node optionality, leaving them exposed to inventory corrections or design-win losses if high-end OEMs resume internal advanced-node PMIC development.
